types.name: Visa-free short stay
types.purpose: Short stays for nationalities that do not need a Schengen visa (e.g. Serbia, the US, the UK).
types.who: Nationals of visa-exempt countries (e.g. Serbia, the US, the UK)
types.note: At most 90 days in any 180-day period across all Schengen countries. Entries and exits are recorded by the Entry/Exit System (EES).

types.name: ETIAS travel authorisation
types.purpose: Online authorisation that visa-free travellers will need before a short stay.
types.who: Nationals of visa-exempt countries, once ETIAS starts
types.note: Not in operation yet — the EU says it starts in the last quarter of 2026. Not a visa; the 90/180 rule still applies.

types.name: Uniform Schengen visa (type C)
types.purpose: Short stays for tourism, business, family visits or events in the Schengen area.
types.who: Nationals of countries that need a Schengen visa
types.maxValidity: Up to 5 years (multiple entry, issued step by step)
types.note: Never more than 90 days in any 180-day period, whatever the visa validity says.

types.name: Visa with limited territorial validity (LTV)
types.purpose: Exceptional short-stay visa valid only for the Schengen country (or countries) named on it.
types.who: Exceptional cases decided by one Schengen country
types.note: Valid only in the countries printed on the visa sticker.

types.name: Airport transit visa (type A)
types.purpose: Changing planes in the international zone of a Schengen airport — for nationalities that need it.
types.who: Nationals of countries on the airport-transit list
types.note: Does not allow entry into the Schengen area.

types.name: National long-stay visa (type D)
types.purpose: Stays over 90 days in one Schengen country (study, work, family), issued by that country under its own rules.
types.who: Anyone with a long-stay reason accepted by that country
types.note: Also allows up to 90 days in any 180 in the other Schengen countries while valid. Rules differ per issuing country.

types.name: Residence permit of a Schengen country
types.purpose: Living in a Schengen country (work, study, family, long-term residence, EU Blue Card).
types.who: Anyone granted residence by a Schengen country
types.note: No day count in the issuing country; up to 90 days in any 180 in the other Schengen countries.
